record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Let r = d - (1 + n) and assume ((n - 1)(n - 2))/6 + 2 < r <= binom(n + 1, 2). For algebras with Hilbert function (1, n, r), decide for which pairs (n, d) the very compressed locus VC_{n,d} is a component and for which it lies in the smoothable component.

evidence.quote: Problem XVI (Shafarevich’s gap, algebras with Hilbert function (1, n, r)). Let r = d − (1 + n) and assume that (n−1)(n−2)/6 + 2 < r ≤ (n+1 choose 2). Decide for which (n, d) the locus VCn,d is a component or lies in the smoothable component.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $0$. For a finite local $k$-algebra $A$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, the Hilbert function of $A$ is the sequence $H_A(i) = \dim_k(\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1})$. Fix integers $n \geq 2$ and $r \geq 1$. A local algebra $A$ of length $d = 1 + n + r$ is said to have Hilbert function $(1,n,r)$ if $\dim_k A/\mathfrak{m} = 1$, $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2 = n$, $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}^2/\mathfrak{m}^3 = r$ and $\mathfrak{m}^3 = 0$. Such an algebra is called very compressed when its Hilbert function is $(1,n,r)$ with $r \leq \binom{n+1}{2}$ (i.e., $\mathfrak{m}^2$ is as large as possible subject to $\mathfrak{m}^3=0$ and the embedding dimension being $n$).

Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parameterizing length-$d$ zero-dimensional subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$. Inside this scheme, let $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d} \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the closure of the locus of points corresponding to (subschemes supported at a single point and isomorphic to) very compressed local algebras with Hilbert function $(1,n,r)$, where $r = d - (1+n)$. The smoothable component is the closure of the open locus parameterizing reduced subschemes (equivalently, the unique irreducible component containing the locus of $d$ distinct points).

Assume that
$$\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{6} + 2 < r \leq \binom{n+1}{2}.$$
Determine, for each such pair $(n,d)$ with $d = 1 + n + r$, whether $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ distinct from the smoothable component, or whether $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d}$ is contained in the smoothable component.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in general. Recent work (a 2025 preprint on components of Hilbert schemes of low degree) resolves specific small cases — showing for instance that the only elementary components of $\mathrm{Hilb}_9$ and $\mathrm{Hilb}_{10}$ on $\mathbb{A}^n$ are those parameterizing algebras with Hilbert functions $(1,5,3)$ and $(1,6,3)$, and that local algebras of degree $9, 10$ with socle dimension $2$ are smoothable — but does not give a full classification across the Shafarevich-gap range.

status_evidence.title: Components of Hilbert Schemes of low degree and smoothable algebras
status_evidence.snippet: The only elementary components of Hilb_9 and Hilb_10 on A^n are the components parameterizing algebras with Hilbert function (1,5,3) and (1,6,3), respectively; any finite local algebra of degrees 9, 10 and socle dimension 2 is smoothable.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific small-degree cases (d=9,10) are resolved; the general Shafarevich gap classification remains open.

status_evidence.title: New elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of new elementary (non-smoothable) components of Hilbert schemes; classification of components in the (1,n,r) range is incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research continues to construct new components, indicating the gap classification is not fully settled.
